title: Compassion and Mercy
definition: Compassion and Mercy are Christlike responses of tender concern and practical care toward those who are suffering, weak, guilty, or in need.
summary: Compassion and Mercy are Christlike responses of tender concern and practical care toward those who are suffering, weak, guilty, or in need.
christFocus: Jesus is moved with compassion, receives sinners, heals the broken, and teaches His people to show mercy as they have received mercy.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Compassion sees suffering and moves toward it rather than turning away. Mercy responds to need with kindness, patience, forgiveness, and practical help.

Scripture grounds compassion in the character of God and the ministry of Christ. Believers show mercy because they have received mercy.

Compassion does not remove truth. Christlike mercy speaks truth with tenderness and serves people without treating them as projects.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many outcast, disabled, addicted, grieving, or church-hurt people have been looked past instead of loved. Compassion and mercy reveal the heart of Christ through His people.

This doctrine also confronts hard-hearted religion that values correctness while neglecting love.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask Christ to give you His eyes for people around you. Move toward someone in need with prayer, patience, practical help, and truth spoken in love.
